notes.trap: `bitmap_count(...)` counts set bits in the raw bytes of a BINARY value. It does not count hex digits or distinct values. X '1010' is the bytes 0x10 0x10, which have only 2 set bits.

`hll_sketch_estimate(...)` takes the binary sketch produced by `hll_sketch_agg(...)` or `hll_union(...)`, not the raw column. NULL inputs are skipped when the sketch is built, so they never count as a distinct value.
`input_file_block_length(...)` returns -1, not NULL or an error, when the row does not come from a file scan. Examples are literals, VALUES lists, or the result after a shuffle.
`java_method(...)` (alias `reflect(...)`) always returns STRING, whatever the Java method's return type is. Cast the result back if you need a number.
IDs are unique but not consecutive, because the partition id sits in the upper 31 bits. Do not use it as a dense row number; use `row_number(...)` instead. Only rows in partition 0 start at 0.
